Content:
Similarly,

Content:

items.title: Converting a Negative Fractional Exponent to a Radical

sections.normalized_html:
Remember that, in general, a negative exponent can be converted to a positive exponent if we take the reciprocal. Here, we have

[MATH: x^{-1/2} = \dfrac{1}{x^{1/2}}.]

Now, we can proceed as usual to convert the fractional exponent to a radical

[MATH: \dfrac{1}{x^{1/2}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}}.]

Therefore, we have

[MATH: x^{-1/2} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}}.]

items.title: Converting a Radical to a Negative Fractional Exponent

sections.normalized_html:
First, we convert the radical to a fractional exponent:

[MATH: \dfrac{1}{\sqrt[3\phantom{|}]{2y}} = \dfrac{1}{(2y)^{1/3}}]

Then, we take the reciprocal and convert the exponent to a negative exponent:

[MATH: \dfrac{1}{(2y)^{1/3}} = (2y)^{-1/3}]

Therefore, we have:

[MATH: \dfrac{1}{\sqrt[3\phantom{|}]{2y}} = (2y)^{-1/3}]
